name: Dis Pater

attributes.attribute: a Latin name meaning Father of Hell
given by Julius Caesar to an unknown Celtic god
a beautiful and timeless Celtic realm, unlike a place of torment

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Dis Pater, also written Dispater or Dis, is a Latin name Julius Caesar gave to a god he believed ruled his Celtic enemies. The name means Father of Hell. The Celts held no idea of a place of torment, so Caesar likely misread them. He also imagined their pantheon mirrored Rome, with central rule and an order of precedence. Scholars nominate three gods for the name, the hammer god known as Sucellus or Taranis, the horned god Cernunnos, and the woodland god Esus, whom Romans called Silvanus. The true god may have ruled the Otherworld, a rich domain of the gods. Far from a place of distress, that realm was beautiful and timeless, and Aeracura appears as Dis Pater's partner.

okr.objective: Examine the Latin name Dis Pater and the unnamed Celtic god behind it.
key_results: The name means Father of Hell
